newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico cocoa Assn head sees output above 50,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Mexico cocoa Assn head sees output above 50,000 T.

text.p: The president of the National Association of Cocoa Producers estimated this week that Mexico's 1996-97 harvest will end between 50,000 and 55,000 tonnes.

In an interview with Reuters, Laurence Rodriguez Torruco said his estimates were based on the production to date of 36,000 tonnes in the cycle's March-October harvesting period and favorable weather conditions.

Mexico's cocoa production swings traditionally between around 30,000 tonnes in poor cycles and 47,000 tonnes in good cycles, according to trade and government sources. The Agriculture Ministry does not publish cocoa output data.
Rodriguez Torruco said favorable weather patterns were largely behind his anticipated spike in production this cycle.
In 95-96, Mexico's cocoa crop was one of the lowest recorded, hit by damage and fallout from from the hurricanes Roxanne and Opal.
Around 80 percent of the national crop is grown in the southern state of Tabasco and almost all the remainder in the neighboring state of Chiapas. Villahermosa is the state capital of Tabsaco.

Rodriguez Torruco said growers focus on supplying cocoa for the national market. The main buyers are Compania Nestle, the Mexican unit of Swiss-based Nestle, and Empresas La Corona, a unit of Mexican food firm Grupo Corvi GCl1.MX. Mexico also exports cocoa.
